alex: heads-up — hitting OOM in a customer integration when consuming SSE with the Python SDK. repro when downstream processing is slow (DB writes). Anyone seen memory growth even though we queue work with a bounded asyncio.Queue?

irene: can you paste the minimal repro? queue maxsize set? what HTTP client?

alex: minimal outline below. using aiohttp + resp.content.iter_chunked(1024) and putting parsed objects into an asyncio.Queue(maxsize=200). consumer does await queue.get() -> write to DB (slow). memory keeps growing over minutes. no token refresh or reconnect happening.

alex: ```python
async with session.get(url) as resp:
    decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
    buf = ''
    dec = json.JSONDecoder()
    async for chunk in resp.content.iter_chunked(1024):
        text = decoder.decode(chunk)
        buf += text
        while True:
            try:
                obj, idx = dec.raw_decode(buf)
            except ValueError:
                break
            await out_q.put(obj)  # bounded queue
            buf = buf[idx:].lstrip()
```

alex: suspecting socket keeps reading even when our queue is full, so in-memory buffer grows.

sasha: yup — aiohttp (and asyncio) will keep feeding the StreamReader unless you explicitly pause the transport. putting into a full queue doesn't stop the underlying read. two routes: 1) use transport.pause_reading()/resume_reading() when queue is full, or 2) backpressure at parse time by awaiting queue.put() *and* pausing the reader until queue has space.

leo: example pattern we've used: check queue.full(), then call resp.connection.transport.pause_reading(); await queue.put(item); if queue.qsize() < threshold: resp.connection.transport.resume_reading(). ugly but effective. watch out for attribute access across aiohttp versions (resp.connection may be None for some reconnects).

tim: another safer approach: use a separate consumer task that writes to DB and have the reader await queue.put() (which will block when full). but that doesn't stop OS from reading into Python buffers — the socket will still be drained into StreamReader. so pause_reading is required for true flow control.

alex: good point re: versions. also ran into unicode split issues where chunk boundary splits a multibyte char and immediate decode() raises. using incremental UTF-8 decoder avoids that (see codecs.getincrementaldecoder).

alex: updated snippet with backpressure + incremental decode:```python
decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
buf = ''
for chunk in resp.content.iter_chunked(1024):
    text = decoder.decode(chunk)
    buf += text
    while True:
        try:
            obj, idx = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(buf)
        except ValueError:
            break
        # if queue is full, pause socket to stop memory growth
        if out_q.full():
            try:
                resp.connection.transport.pause_reading()
            except Exception:
                pass
        await out_q.put(obj)
        if not out_q.full():
            try:
                resp.connection.transport.resume_reading()
            except Exception:
                pass
        buf = buf[idx:].lstrip()
```
